input.quote: Ono shall have the right, in accordance with this Section 2.2, to grant sublicenses under the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates and to Third Parties, provided that Ono shall not engage a Third Party as either (i) a Sublicensee of the Product, or (ii) as a distributor of the Product, without Array's prior written consent.
input.rationale: The grant to us in Section 2.1 is an exclusive (development/commercialization) and worldwide non-exclusive (manufacturing) licence with express sublicensing rights, and it reaches our Affiliates and contractors: Section 2.2(a) lets us sublicense to Affiliates without Array consent, Section 2.1(b) confirms the manufacturing licence "may be extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf," and Section 1.57 recognises that a Party or its Affiliate may subcontract performance of activities under the Agreement. The licence is not revocable at Array's discretion — Array may terminate only for uncured material breach (13.3, 90/60-day cure) or bankruptcy (13.4), and on expiry the Section 2.1 licences become "fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights" (13.1). Section 18.9 permits assignment without consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of our business or assets, satisfying the successor-transfer requirement. This meets the preferred position; the only sub-element short of ideal is that engaging a Third Party Sublicensee or distributor needs Array's prior written consent without an express reasonableness qualifier, which is customary in a pharma territory licence and is noted rather than redlined.
